content: In a verso document, I'd like to be able to create links that are relative to a base location, where the base location is passed to the main verso executable as a parameter. Is this possible? It seems like this would require having that parameter be part of the verso state that could be accessed within the link.

Can you say a bit more about the use case? Which genre are you working in?

Right now, Verso-generated HTML is intended to have all site-local URLs be relative to the root of the site itself, with a <base> tag that points to the site's root. That way, we can emit them consistently on all pages, and sites work properly when hosted under a URL prefix. Overriding this base is one way to get what you're looking for.

But if you instead want this to be the case only for some links, then it's necessary to get the data some other way. We don't presently have a way to add arbitrary parameters to a site in any of the genres, but this could be possible.

Is it important that it's a command-line parameter? If you can set environment variables instead, then this should be pretty easy to accomplish today with no new features.

I'm working on a document that explains the internals of Lean. I use the versotreedoc tool in https://github.com/richardlford/versotreedoc to generate the verso files that mirror the files being documented. The links I want to create are "vscode:" protocol links that can link, either to the code being documented, or to the verso source file that will hold the documentation. This makes it possible, when browsing the document, to open, in vscode, either of the corresponding files. Here is an example:

-- /home/fordrl/e/lean4internals/Vtd_mods/Vtd_verso/Vtd_src/Vtd_verso/Vtd_Verso/Vtd_CLI.lean.lean



import VersoManual
open Verso.Genre Manual
open Verso.Genre.Manual.InlineLean

#doc (Manual) "`m/v/s/verso/Verso/CLI.lean`"  =>

%%%
authors := ["Richard L Ford"]
tag := "mods-verso-src-verso-Verso-CLI-lean"
%%%

[source](vscode:/home/fordrl/e/lean4internals/mods/verso/src/verso/Verso/CLI.lean) [doc-source](vscode:/home/fordrl/e/lean4internals/Vtd_mods/Vtd_verso/Vtd_src/Vtd_verso/Vtd_Verso/Vtd_CLI.lean.lean)

A couple of simple functions to aid in parsing options, specifically that an
option that requires a filename has one provided.

As you can see, I currently have absolute path names, but I'd like them to be relative. It would be sufficient for them to be relative to the cwd when the verso executable ran.

The base does not need to be from the command line. An environment variable would work.

My current version of the lean internals document is located at https://github.com/richardlford/lean4internals.

If these links could be made relative, then it would be possible to make the writing of the Lean internals document collaborative, and different people could work on documenting different parts.

The idea of the links is to make it easy to edit the document by providing links both to the artifact being documented, and to the source of the documenting document. So what is needed in order to make the links relative is the root of the artifact source being documented, and the root of the documenting document. In my case, I decided to have the artifacts being documented to be git submodules of the documenting document, so that their source is locally available.

Making links relative to the cwd of the process should be fairly easy to do.

What about a syntax like:

Here's a {srclink "mods/verso/src/verso/Verso/CLI.lean"}[source] link

Here's a quick sketch of an implementation, because I am a bit short on time right now, but if it's not enough let me know and I can flesh it out:

structure SrcLink where
  path : String

instance : FromArgs SrcLink m where
  fromArgs := SrcLink.mk <$> .positional'

@[role]
def srclink : RoleExpanderOf SrcLink
  | { path }, args =>
    -- TODO: check that file exists, warn/error if not
    ``(Inline.link $(quote <| "vscode:" ++ path) #[$[$(args.mapM elabInline)],*])

I will give that a try. Another idea I had is that if there was something like this:

{env}`ARTIFACT_ROOT`

that would read the ARTIFACT_ROOT environment variable and substitute in its value, then that could be used to get base locations.

Here is a version that I got to work:

import Verso
import VersoManual.InlineLean.Signature

open Verso ArgParse Doc
open Lean Elab

section Slink

variable [Monad m] [MonadInfoTree m] [MonadLiftT CoreM m] [MonadEnv m] [MonadError m]


structure SrcLink where
  path : String

instance : FromArgs SrcLink m where
  fromArgs := SrcLink.mk  <$> positional' `path

@[role]
def srclink : RoleExpanderOf SrcLink
  | { path }, args => do
    let fsPath := System.FilePath.mk path
    let cwd ← IO.currentDir
    let absPath := if fsPath.isRelative then System.FilePath.mk (s!"{cwd}" ++ "/" ++ path) else fsPath
    let isFile := (← absPath.pathExists) && ! (← absPath.isDir)
    if ! isFile then
      throwError s!"{path} interpreted as {absPath} either does not exist or is not a file."
    ``(Inline.link #[$[$(← args.mapM elabInline)],*] $(quote <| "vscode:" ++ s!"{absPath}" ))

end Slink

I just put the above in a local Myextensions.lean file and imported and it works, but the file has to be imported into every file that uses it. Is this something that would be worth adding to verso?

I leave absolute paths unchanged, but for relative paths I prepend the CWD. I check that the
resulting path exists and is a file.

Thanks for the pointer.

I also experimented with a version that take the name of an environment variable and uses its value as a base. That also worked. It would be useful if you wanted the base location of the artifact being documented to be outside the tree holding the documenting document.

Great to see that you got it to work!

Because Verso files are just Lean files, it's expected that you have to import the definitions of functions that you call. What I usually do is make a "meta" module for each document that re-exports all the helpers that I've defined for the document, so I just import that at the top of each file.

I think that this is a specific-enough use case that it probably doesn't make sense to add it to Verso. Part of the point of Verso is that users can implement whatever is not provided out of the box :-)

For now I've made a module, VersoExts, that I've placed in https://github.com/richardlford/versoexts, that I can require and import in my projects. I can use that to place experimental extensions. If any of them should be considered generally useful at some point they could be migrated into Verso. Thanks for your help.
My next plan is to study Verso in more detail. I have a feeling there are more features that are not yet in the manual and I'd like to learn about them and possibly contribute to the manual.
There are indeed such features! Thank you!
